subject: Lindsay Clancy to face retrial next year for deaths of her three children
posts:
A Massachusetts judge schedules Lindsay Clancy's retrial for March following a hung jury in her first murder trial.
Evidence: Court scheduling, mistrial record
#Law #News 🌐

Lindsay Clancy will face a retrial in March on murder charges for the deaths of her three children after jurors deadlocked.

=== MULTI-SOURCE TOPIC CLUSTER: Lindsay Clancy to face retrial next year for deaths of her three children ===

[Source 1 — www.bbc.co.uk (Bias: Center / Public Broadcaster)] (URL: https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cw5y1v8de35go?at_medium=RSS&at_campaign=rss):
Lindsay Clancy to face retrial next year for deaths of her three children

The 36-year-old's first trial this year fell apart when a 12-person jury failed to reach a verdict.

[Source 2 — www.cbc.ca (Bias: Center / Public Broadcaster)] (URL: https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/lindsay-clancy-court-trial-9.7423387?cmp=rss):
Lindsay Clancy will be retried in March for the killing of her 3 children

Lindsay Clancy, the Massachusetts mother whose highly divisive murder trial shone a global spotlight on postpartum mental health, will be tried again on murder charges for the killings of her three children.

[Source 3 — www.theguardian.com (Bias: Left / Progressive)] (URL: https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/16/lindsay-clancy-retrial-march):
Judge sets Lindsay Clancy retrial for March in killings of her three children

Clancy’s first trial on charges of first-degree murder ended in mistrial after jurors couldn’t reach unanimous verdict A Massachusetts judge on Monday scheduled Lindsay Clancy’s second trial in the killings of her three young children for late March, over the objections of prosecutors.Clancy was charged with three counts of first-degree murder. Her first trial ended in a mistrial after jurors were unable to reach a unanimous verdict on whether she was criminally responsible for the killings. Eleven jurors favored acquittal on the grounds of insanity, while one disagreed. Continue reading...
